purpose: Per CEO R294 P1: 'Build a full commercial dossier skeleton for P-02 through P-15. Every candidate needs the same minimum package: 15 elements. P-01 is the reference implementation.'
constitutional_basis: Article X (canonical state). Article XXVIII (honest evidence state per candidate).
design_principle: Every candidate gets the same 15-element structure. The CONTENT differs. The STRUCTURE is identical. This makes the portfolio machine-processable: the optimizer can compare any candidate on any dimension.

maturity_states.definition: DISCOVERED → COMMERCIALIZED → TECHNICALLY_SPECIFIED → VALIDATION_READY → INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED → ECONOMICALLY_PROVEN → BUYER_READY → PILOT → TRANSACTION
maturity_states.rule: Each candidate has exactly one maturity state. State transitions require new evidence (Article XXVIII).

buyer_proof_economics_5_tier.tier_1_target_price: Internal target — what WE think the package is worth
buyer_proof_economics_5_tier.tier_2_expected_buyer_value: What the buyer SHOULD save/earn if the technology works
buyer_proof_economics_5_tier.tier_3_buyer_indicated_wtp: What a buyer SAYS they would pay (from buyer questionnaire)
buyer_proof_economics_5_tier.tier_4_actual_offer: What a buyer actually OFFERS in negotiation
buyer_proof_economics_5_tier.rule: Tiers 1-2 are MODELLED. Tier 3 is BUYER_EVIDENCE. Tiers 4-5 are TRANSACTIONS. The machine must never conflate them.

dossiers.name: Rate-Limited Physiologic Conductance Control
dossiers.1_mechanism: Bounded-rate (2%/sec) conductance slew for multi-segment hydraulic drainage with sensor-health fallback
dossiers.2_architecture: 4-segment parallel drainage, variable-orifice valves, pressure+flow sensors, central controller
dossiers.6_known_evidence: 225-run ablation (rate limiting confirmed 41/45), 180-run canonical comparison (V2.1 beats B 9/9 attacks), FDA PCLC metrics, VIEshunt comparison, cross-domain research
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Physical bench validation, independent lab replication, buyer-verified economics, live patent search by attorney
dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: US20210338992A1, US20260115436A1, WO2025076272A1, VIEshunt. Our argument: bounded RATE (not just fallback) + multi-segment redistribution = novel combination producing measurable 2-3x advantage
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Miethke SENSOR RESERVOIR + P-01 control law = closed-loop adaptive shunt. Also: Medtronic Codman, Integra, Sophysa
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Miethke: upgrade SENSOR RESERVOIR from monitoring-only to closed-loop control using V2.1 algorithm
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: Build physical bench ($7-10K). Run 80-run blinded protocol. Send to Miethke.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Technical evaluation → bench results → buyer feedback → V2.2 if needed → economic questionnaire → IP assessment by buyer counsel → transaction negotiation

dossiers.name: Neuromorphic Failure Predictor
dossiers.1_mechanism: AI-based implant failure prediction using neuromorphic (event-driven) computing for ultra-low-power real-time prediction on-implant
dossiers.2_architecture: Neuromorphic chip (e.g., Intel Loihi 2 or simulation) + trained SNN model + implant sensor data input + failure probability output
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — needs dataset identification first
dossiers.4_prototype_blueprint: NOT STARTED — depends on dataset availability
dossiers.5_test_protocol: NOT STARTED — needs dataset + model baseline first
dossiers.6_known_evidence: NONE — concept only. Portfolio optimizer identifies this as quick-win IF public dataset exists.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Dataset identification, license verification, baseline model training, accuracy comparison (neuromorphic vs cloud ML), power analysis, buyer interest validation

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Implant revision surgery $30-50K per event. If predictor prevents 20% of failures: $6-10M/yr per 1000 patients

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: cloud-based ML prediction (2023 PubMed study, 33K patients, ROC AUC 0.733). Our argument: on-implant neuromorphic prediction eliminates cloud latency, privacy concerns, and connectivity dependency. Ultra-low-power enables chronic implantation.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Medtronic (cardiac implant monitoring), Abbott (CGM+implant), Boston Scientific (CRM devices). Could integrate into any implantable device with failure prediction needs.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Medtronic: add failure prediction to implantable cardiac devices (ICD, pacemaker) without increasing battery drain. Currently requires cloud-connected data upload.
dossiers.12_buyer_evaluation_kit: NOT STARTED — needs dataset validation first
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: IDENTIFY DATASET: search for public implant failure datasets (MIMIC-IV, FDA MAUDE, Hydrocephalus Clinical Research Network, National Surgical Quality Improvement Program). Verify license, endpoints, sample size. If no dataset exists, P-13 EV drops and optimizer re-ranks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Dataset → baseline model → neuromorphic comparison → power analysis → buyer approach → technical evaluation → transaction

dossiers.name: Phage-Based Anti-Biofilm Defense
dossiers.1_mechanism: Bacteriophage coating on implant surfaces that prevents biofilm formation through targeted bacterial lysis without antibiotics
dossiers.2_architecture: Phage-immobilized surface coating on orthopedic implant (joint replacement, spinal hardware). Phages target common biofilm-forming bacteria (S. aureus, S. epidermidis).
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — needs phage selection and immobilization chemistry first
dossiers.4_prototype_blueprint: NOT STARTED — needs in vitro demonstration first
dossiers.5_test_protocol: NOT STARTED — needs phage candidates identified first
dossiers.6_known_evidence: NONE — concept only. Literature review needed.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Phage candidate selection, immobilization chemistry, in vitro biofilm prevention assay, biocompatibility, regulatory pathway (phage = biologic? combination product?)

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Implant infection costs $50-100K per case (revision surgery + antibiotics + hospital stay). 1-5% infection rate. If phage coating prevents 50%: $250K-2.5M/yr per 1000 implants

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: antibiotic-loaded bone cement, silver coatings, chlorhexidine. Our argument: phage coating targets specific bacteria without contributing to antibiotic resistance. Phage therapy is FDA-approved for compassionate use. Novel application to implant coating.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Stryker (joint replacement coating), Zimmer Biomet (joint+spine), J&J DePuy Synthes (trauma+spine), Smith+Nephew (joint). Could coat ANY orthopedic implant.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Stryker: coat Triathlon knee implant with phage against S. aureus. Reduces 1-5% infection rate. Differentiates from competitor coatings (antibiotic/silver).
dossiers.12_buyer_evaluation_kit: NOT STARTED — needs literature review first
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: LITERATURE REVIEW: identify 3-5 bacteriophage species effective against S. aureus biofilm. Identify immobilization chemistry candidates. Assess regulatory pathway (FDA phage guidance). Cost: $5-15K, 2-4 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Literature → phage candidates → in vitro design → buyer approach (Stryker biomaterials) → technical evaluation → transaction

dossiers.name: Pulsation-Synchronized Catalytic Contact-Time Lock
dossiers.1_mechanism: CSF flow modulation synchronized with cardiac pulsation to maximize enzymatic contact time for amyloid/tau clearance
dossiers.2_architecture: Enzymatic membrane + pulsation-synchronized flow modulator + controller (reuses P-01 hardware)
dossiers.4_prototype_blueprint: V1 engineering-only prototype ready ($5-15K, 4-8 weeks). V2 with enzyme blocked.
dossiers.5_test_protocol: Phase 1 wet-lab protocol COMPLETE (7 steps, 3 months, $40-80K). Collaborator package COMPLETE.
dossiers.6_known_evidence: Engineering frozen. Biology unfrozen. CSF Aβ << NEP Km (mass-transport limited). Phase 1 protocol pre-registered.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Enzyme identity, immobilization, kinetics, CSF stability (Phase 1-3 wet-lab). Independent validation. Buyer economics.

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Leqembi costs $50-200K/patient/year. If CSF clearance achieves 20% of effect: $10-40K/patient/year value

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: US20090131850A1 (CSF protein filtration), US11529443 (Aβ/tau membrane). Our argument: pulsation-synchronized contact-time lock is the differentiator.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: AbbVie (Leqembi), Eli Lilly, Denali, Alector. Also shunt OEMs (Medtronic, Integra) for hardware integration.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: AbbVie: dual-function shunt (drainage + amyloid clearance) for NPH patients with Alzheimer's comorbidity. Eliminates IV Leqembi infusion for this population.
dossiers.12_buyer_evaluation_kit: NOT STARTED — needs Phase 1 wet-lab results first
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: Engage enzyme engineering collaborator. Send COLLABORATOR_COMPLETE_PACKAGE.json to 3-5 labs (MIT BME, Stanford BME, Rice BME, Northwestern BME, WuXi AppTec).
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Collaborator → Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → buyer approach → transaction

dossiers.name: Chemical ICP Transduction Platform
dossiers.1_mechanism: ICP-to-chemical molecular signal transduction via pressure-responsive molecule release, detected by wearable biosensor — zero electronics in brain
dossiers.2_architecture: Transducer (implant) + CSF transport + wearable biosensor + inverse reconstruction model
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — molecule unspecified (9-step path, 0/9 resolved)
dossiers.6_known_evidence: Architecture concept. 9-step molecule-selection research program defined. 5 candidate molecule classes identified.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Molecule design (12-24 months, $1-5M). All 9 specification steps. 20-40% success probability.

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Eliminates battery replacement surgery ($15-30K every 5-10 yr). $267M/yr if 100K patients.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: RF telemetry ICP implants (Raumedic, Codman). Our argument: zero electronics in brain — genuinely new communication channel. Prior art search needed (training-knowledge only, not live).
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Raumedic, Codman/Integra, Sophysa, Miethke. Also: Dexcom/Abbott (biosensor expertise), VC firms (research funding).
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Raumedic: replace Neurovent (battery-powered telemetric ICP) with zero-electronics chemical transduction. Eliminates battery replacement surgery.
dossiers.12_buyer_evaluation_kit: NOT STARTED — research collaboration / development option only
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: Engage medicinal chemistry consultant. Execute molecule-selection Step 1 (candidate mechanisms, $200-500K, 14 months).
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Research collaboration → molecule discovery → bench prototype → buyer approach → transaction (or architecture dies if no molecule found)

dossiers.name: Energy-Neutral Micro-Assist
dossiers.1_mechanism: Energy harvesting from physiological flow/pressure gradients to power implantable sensors without battery replacement
dossiers.2_architecture: Micro-turbine or piezoelectric harvester in CSF/blood flow path + power management circuit + sensor load
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — needs energy budget analysis first
dossiers.6_known_evidence: NONE — concept only. Energy budget analysis is the first test.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Energy budget (available vs required), harvester design, in vitro demonstration, biocompatibility, chronic stability

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Battery replacement surgery $15-30K every 5-10 years. If eliminated: $2-6M/yr per 1000 patients.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: primary cell batteries (Saft LM-175). Research: piezoelectric harvesting in blood flow (literature exists). Our argument: application to CSF shunt flow is novel.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Medtronic, Abbott, Boston Scientific (cardiac implants). Sophysa, Miethke (shunt implants).
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Medtronic: power cardiac implant sensors from blood flow energy harvesting. Eliminates battery replacement in pacemakers/ICDs.
dossiers.12_buyer_evaluation_kit: NOT STARTED — needs energy budget first
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: COMPUTE ENERGY BUDGET: available power from CSF flow (0.3 mL/min at 12 mmHg) or cardiac pulsation. Compare to sensor+controller load (1 mW). If P_available < P_required × 10, EV drops. Cost: $0-5K (computational), 1-2 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Energy budget → feasibility → harvester design → in vitro → buyer approach → transaction

dossiers.name: Selective Fail-Operational Membrane
dossiers.1_mechanism: Membrane geometry that maintains partial filtration when partially occluded — fails operational, not fail-closed
dossiers.2_architecture: Multi-channel membrane with graded pore sizes and flow distribution that preserves partial function under progressive occlusion
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — needs computational model first
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Computational model of fail-operational geometry, in vitro demonstration, manufacturing feasibility

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Membrane failure in medical devices causes total system failure. Graceful degradation extends device life and reduces emergency interventions.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: standard membranes (fail closed). Our argument: graded-pore geometry maintains partial flow under occlusion. Novel membrane architecture.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Pall/Danaher (filtration), Sartorius, 3M, Merck Millipore, Thermo Fisher. Also: implant companies using membranes (Stryker, Medtronic).
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Pall/Danaher: add fail-operational membrane to medical filtration products. Differentiates from standard membranes. Extends filter life.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: BUILD COMPUTATIONAL MODEL: simulate graded-pore membrane under progressive occlusion. Compare flow curves: standard vs fail-operational. Cost: $3-10K, 2-4 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Computational model → in vitro → buyer approach (Pall/Danaher) → transaction

dossiers.name: Self-Powered Physiologic Sensing
dossiers.1_mechanism: Self-powered implantable sensor harvesting energy from physiological motion (cardiac, respiratory) for continuous sensing without battery
dossiers.2_architecture: Piezoelectric or electromagnetic harvester + sensor + power management + telemetry (all implantable, no battery)
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — needs energy budget analysis (similar to P-08)
dossiers.6_known_evidence: NONE — concept only. Related to P-08 (energy harvesting) but focused on sensing rather than general power.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Energy budget from cardiac/respiratory motion, sensor power requirements, harvester design, in vitro demonstration

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Eliminates battery replacement surgery for implantable sensors. $15-30K per surgery avoided.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: battery-powered implantable sensors (Codman MicroSensor, Medtronic Reveal). Research: piezoelectric harvesting literature exists. Our argument: self-powered sensing module for chronic implantation.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Medtronic, Abbott, Boston Scientific, Edwards, Dexcom, Terumo.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Medtronic: self-powered pressure sensor for cardiac implant. Eliminates battery in Reveal LINQ. Or: self-powered ICP sensor (no battery in brain).
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: COMPUTE ENERGY BUDGET from cardiac motion (0.5-2 Hz, 10-30% amplitude) or respiratory motion (0.2 Hz). Compare to sensor load. Cost: $0-5K, 1-2 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Energy budget → feasibility → harvester design → in vitro → buyer approach → transaction

dossiers.name: Enzymatic CSF Clearance (Tau/Alpha-Synuclein)
dossiers.1_mechanism: Enzyme-immobilized module that degrades pathological proteins (tau, alpha-synuclein) during CSF drainage
dossiers.2_architecture: Enzyme-immobilized membrane in shunt drainage path + CSF flow
dossiers.3_engineering_design: NOT STARTED — needs enzyme selection first
dossiers.6_known_evidence: NONE — concept only. Related to P-04 (enzymatic clearance) but targets tau/alpha-synuclein instead of amyloid.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Enzyme selection (tau protease, alpha-synuclein protease), in vitro activity, chronic stability, regulatory pathway

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Parkinson's/Alzheimer's treatment costs $50-200K/patient/year. Local CSF clearance could reduce systemic drug burden.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: IV antibody therapy. No local CSF clearance for tau/alpha-synuclein exists. Our argument: enzyme-immobilized local clearance.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Denali Therapeutics, Alector, AbbVie, Eli Lilly, Biogen, Roche.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Denali: add tau-degrading enzyme to CSF shunt for Parkinson's patients with shunted hydrocephalus. Local clearance reduces systemic drug dose.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: LITERATURE REVIEW: identify tau-degrading enzymes (e.g., cathepsin D, MMP-2). Identify alpha-synuclein-degrading enzymes (e.g., NEP, IDE). Assess feasibility. Cost: $5-20K, 2-4 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Literature → enzyme candidates → in vitro → buyer approach (Denali/Alector) → transaction

dossiers.name: Adaptive Valve Pressure-Response Profile
dossiers.1_mechanism: Adaptive valve that adjusts drainage based on patient-specific intracranial compliance
dossiers.2_architecture: Pressure sensor + compliance estimator + adaptive valve controller
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Compliance estimation algorithm, computational model, bench validation

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Multiple adjustment surgeries cost $30-50K each. If adaptive profiling reduces revisions by 30%: $9-15M/yr per 1000 patients.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: fixed-pressure programmable valves (Codman Hakim, Sophysa Polaris). Our argument: adaptive profiling based on real-time compliance estimation.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Medtronic, Sophysa, Integra, Miethke (shunt valve manufacturers). Also spine companies (Stryker, Globus) for CSF diversion in spine surgery.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Sophysa: upgrade Polaris from fixed-setting to adaptive-setting based on patient compliance. Reduces adjustment surgeries.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: BUILD COMPUTATIONAL MODEL: simulate adaptive profiling vs fixed settings across 10 virtual patient profiles with varying compliance. Cost: $5-15K, 2-4 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Computational model → bench validation → buyer approach → transaction

dossiers.name: Washout-Gated Drug Release
dossiers.1_mechanism: CSF flow-gated drug release that delivers therapeutic agents proportional to drainage rate
dossiers.2_architecture: Flow sensor + flow-gated release mechanism + drug reservoir
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Flow-gated release kinetics model, in vitro demonstration, drug stability in CSF

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Intrathecal pumps cost $50-100K + $15-30K/yr drug. If flow-gated release is simpler: significant cost reduction.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: Medtronic SynchroMed (fixed-rate intrathecal pump). Our argument: flow-gated release ties delivery to natural CSF dynamics, preventing over/under-dosing.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Medtronic: add flow-gated release to SynchroMed. Eliminates fixed-rate over/under-dosing. Simplifies pump programming.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: BUILD COMPUTATIONAL MODEL: simulate flow-gated release kinetics vs fixed-rate. Compare drug exposure profiles. Cost: $5-15K, 2-4 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Computational model → in vitro → buyer approach → transaction

dossiers.name: Phase-Change Valve Actuation
dossiers.1_mechanism: Valve actuated by phase-change material (solid-liquid transition) instead of electromechanical actuator
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Material selection (transition near 37°C), power analysis, cycle life, in vitro demonstration

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Electromechanical valves are complex and power-hungry. Phase-change simplifies manufacturing and reduces power.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: solenoid, MEMS, piezoelectric valves. Our argument: phase-change actuation is simpler, lower power, potentially longer cycle life.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Edwards, Medtronic, Abbott, Sophysa, Miethke, Cook Medical, Terumo.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Edwards: simplify heart valve actuation mechanism. Or: Miethke: simplify shunt valve adjustment mechanism.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: LITERATURE REVIEW: identify phase-change materials with transition temperature near 37°C. Compute power comparison vs solenoid. Cost: $3-10K, 2-3 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Literature → material selection → power analysis → in vitro → buyer approach → transaction

dossiers.name: Residual Conductance Floor (Safety Module)
dossiers.1_mechanism: Hard minimum drainage guarantee preventing complete flow collapse under conservative controller behavior
dossiers.2_architecture: Safety module integrated into P-01 controller architecture
dossiers.3_engineering_design: PARTIAL — defined as P-01 module (drainage floor = 50% of target, ablation evidence available)
dossiers.6_known_evidence: Ablation evidence: drainage floor is non-critical on most attacks but HELPS on sensor_dropout (2.98x ratio). V2.2 design insight: relax during dropout.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Standalone commercial viability (likely bundled with P-01)

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Prevents over-cautious controller from causing under-drainage. Safety feature.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: No existing drainage floor mechanism in current shunts. Part of P-01's architecture.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Bundled with P-01. Safety module for P-01's rate-limited controller.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: NONE standalone — validate as part of P-01 bench

dossiers.name: Drainage-Priority Clearance (Safety Module)
dossiers.1_mechanism: Controlled release that prioritizes CSF drainage over therapeutic clearance (safety-first for combination products)
dossiers.2_architecture: Safety controller module for P-04 combination product
dossiers.3_engineering_design: PARTIAL — defined as P-04 safety module (drainage floor = 0.10 mL/min hard floor)
dossiers.6_known_evidence: Drainage floor specified (0.10 mL/min). Fail-safe bypass defined.
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Standalone commercial viability (likely bundled with P-04)

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Regulatory safety feature for combination products. Prevents therapeutic function from compromising drainage.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: No existing drainage-priority module for combination shunts. Part of P-04 architecture.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Bundled with P-04. Safety module for P-04's dual-function shunt.
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: NONE standalone — validate as part of P-04 wet-lab

dossiers.name: Production-Matched Drainage
dossiers.1_mechanism: Real-time CSF production estimation that matches drainage rate to actual production, maintaining zero net flow balance
dossiers.2_architecture: Production estimator (from ICP recovery dynamics) + drainage rate controller
dossiers.6_known_evidence: NONE — skeleton only. Related to P-01 (could be a module of P-01's controller).
dossiers.7_missing_evidence: Production estimation algorithm, computational model, validation against physiological data

8_economic_model.tier_2_buyer_value: Over/under-drainage from fixed drainage costs $30-50K per revision. Production-matched drainage could prevent 20% of revisions.

dossiers.9_prior_art_argument: Existing: fixed-rate drainage (all current shunts). US12636471 (2026) covers CSF metering. Our argument: production-matched (not just metered) drainage.
dossiers.10_buyer_integration: Medtronic, Integra, Sophysa, Miethke. Could be a module of P-01.
dossiers.11_buyer_use_case: Medtronic: add production-matched drainage to P-01 controller. Prevents over-drainage at night (low production) and under-drainage during exercise (high production).
dossiers.14_next_evidence_action: BUILD CSF PRODUCTION ESTIMATOR: estimate production from ICP recovery dynamics. Test against 10 virtual patient profiles. Cost: $5-15K, 2-4 weeks.
dossiers.15_transaction_path: Computational model → validation → buyer approach → transaction (or bundle with P-01)
